newsitem.title: TRINIDAD AND TOBAGO: Shooting at sea sours Trinidad-Venezuela relations.
newsitem.headline: Shooting at sea sours Trinidad-Venezuela relations.

text.p: The Trinidad and Tobago government has protested to Venezuela over the shooting of a Trinidadian trawler skipper in an incident involving the Venezuelan Coast Guard.

Foreign Minister Ralph Maraj told Parliament on Friday talks on cooperation between the two countries would be suspended pending a resolution to the incident in which Ralpheus Lewis, 44, was shot and wounded while shrimping in the Gulf of Paria.
Negotiations over a new fishing treaty scheduled to have started last Thursday have been suspended indefinitely.
Maraj summoned Venezuela's ambassador in Port of Spain, Freddy Christians, on Friday and handed over a protest letter.
"We must get down to the bottom of this incident before there is any further cooperation between us," he said.
"The Trinidad and Tobago government will not allow our fishermen to be shot at, killed or taken advantage of."
Lewis and four crewmen were shrimping in what they said were Trinidad's waters when they were attacked last Wednesday.
Venezuelan Foreign Minister Angel Burelli Rivas first protested the incident, saying the coast guard vessel Magarita was in Venezuelan waters when it was rammed by the trawler, the Hannah.
The waters of the Gulf of Paria are rich shrimping grounds. But they are also used by drug traffickers and see frequent conflicts between fishermen from both countries.
Several Trinidadians have been killed in the gulf, reportedly by Venezuelans. In an incident two weeks ago, one Trinidadian was found murdered aboard his boat.
